[0] everyday_reading (E): Everyday "rank" means a position in a list (1st, 2nd) and "frequency" a rate; here a page's rank is a probability, estimated by the fraction freq[i]/T of moves that land on it.
[1] misconception (M) -> FewTrialsAreExact: wrong rule: A short simulation gives the exact page ranks. Right rule: freq[i]/T is only an estimate: about 10^n moves for n-digit precision and many more for accuracy.
[2] misconception (M) -> ManyDigitsMeanAccurate: wrong rule: A result printed with many decimal places must be accurate to those places. Right rule: Printing %8.5f does not make the estimate accurate to 5 places; ensuring accuracy is often the hardest part.
[3] inconsistent_trace (T) -> FewTrialsAreExact: Applies LT (increment after each move, divide by T after the loop) unevenly: e.g. incrementing the page before the move on some passes, or dividing inside the loop. (here mixing in: "A short simulation gives the exact page ranks")

[0] names_the_element (N): A counting technique: an int array freq[] with one counter per page, incremented each time the surfer lands there; dividing by T gives the visit frequencies.
[1] states_the_rule (S): RandomSurfer counts the number of times the surfer visits each page; dividing that count by the number of moves estimates the probability of ending on the page (its rank).

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): freq is created (all zeros) before the loop; each pass ends with freq[page]++; after the loop, each (double) freq[i] / T is computed (cast first, then divide) and printed.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Integer counts summing to T; the printed fractions are doubles in [0, 1] summing to about 1 (e.g. 0.27280 0.26530 0.14820 0.24830 0.06540 after 10000 moves).
[2] one_step_execution (OS): One count step adds 1 to exactly one element, freq[page]; all other counts are unchanged.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): The increment is the last statement of each pass, so the counts tally the pages reached by the T moves (sum = T).
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): freq[i]/T converges to the same page ranks the power method computes, but only as an estimate.
[2] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Counter plan per bucket (a tally array indexed by outcome): each freq[i] is a gatherer accumulating visits to page i, and the array holds the histogram that stabilises to the ranks.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> FewTrialsAreExact: Invariant: the counts sum to T, so the fractions sum to 1; dividing before casting ((double)(freq[i] / T)) or counting outside the loop breaks it.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use whenever a probability is estimated from repeated random trials (histograms, Monte Carlo); not when the exact probabilities can be computed, as with the power method.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Casting must apply before the division. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: (double) (freq[i] / T) or freq[i] / T: integer division gives 0 for every page that is not visited on every move.
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: A local array must be created before use. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: int[] freq; declared without new int[N] and then incremented: compile error, variable might not have been initialized.

wrong: A result printed with many decimal places must be accurate to those places. | right: A program does not produce accurate answers simply because it can print numbers to many decimal places of precision; ensuring accuracy is often the most difficult challenge.

wrong: A short simulation gives the exact page ranks. | right: A simulation only estimates the page ranks: RandomSurfer needs 10^n moves to get answers precise to n decimal places and many more moves for those answers to become accurate (tens of thousands of moves for two accurate places, millions for three).

Frequency counting keeps one counter per value in an array, freq[page]++.
The visit fractions freq[j] / T estimate the same page ranks that repeated matrix multiplication computes.
On each pass the simulation adds 1 to freq[page] for the page just reached.
